title: 10 Portfolio Red Flags That Instantly Disqualify You (Tech Lead Perspective)
transcript:
Here are the top red flags that make tech leads close your portfolio tab immediately:
Red flag 1: Generic tutorial clones. If your top project is a basic To-Do list, a Netflix clone, or a Weather app with no custom features, it tells the reviewer you can only follow YouTube tutorials. Build real, original tools or solve a niche problem.
Red flag 2: Dead live links. If I click 'Live Demo' and get a 404 or a spinning loader that never finishes, you are instantly disqualified. Verify every deployment link.
Red flag 3: Skill percentage progress bars. Writing 'HTML: 90%, CSS: 85%, JavaScript: 80%, Python: 60%' is completely meaningless. What does 85% CSS even mean? Do you know 85% of the CSS spec? Replace progress bars with real tagged project cards showing the tech in production.
Red flag 4: No GitHub repo or private/empty repos. Tech leads want to inspect your Git commit history, your component architecture, and how clean your code is. Include a direct GitHub link with an exhaustive README.
Red flag 5: Buried contact info. Put your email and social links in the header, in the hero, and in the footer. Do not make people fill out a 7-field contact form just to hire you.
